content:
Rumors were swirling earlier this year that iOS 26.4 would bring a revamped Health app. Then it was delayed, iOS 27 came and went, and the revamp is still nowhere to be found.

With the all-new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to debut next month, it's worth asking: will these new features arrive alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's worth reviewing why these features will likely arrive in September. You might be thinking, "Isn't all software supposed to launch in June?" — but there's precedent for this.

Low Power Mode in watchOS 9, sleep apnea detection in watchOS 11, and hypertension notifications in watchOS 26 all arrived in September, despite not requiring the latest hardware.

So based on all that, Apple is highly likely to wait until September to unveil its latest Health app upgrade, even if the features don't strictly require a new Apple Watch.

Still Time

Ahead of WWDC27, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman warned that the new Health app upgrade, codenamed "Project Mulberry," might not appear at the WWDC keynote. That prediction proved accurate:

Does this mean Project Mulberry is definitely showing up at the September keynote? Not necessarily. But given the precedent of September feature announcements and the fact that we already knew it was coming later than WWDC, a September debut is still quite possible, even if it ultimately arrives in October alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

Rumors about this set of features have gone back and forth, as there are a lot of variables in play. You may have heard about a standalone Health+ service offering doctor-led video content. However, that plan has reportedly been scaled back, with features instead being integrated into the existing Health app experience.

Two things, however, are very clear: there will be an AI health coach that gives you health advice based on your Health app data, and the ability to provide real-time coaching through your camera for exercise and other health-related tasks. Another major part of this upgrade is a brand-new Health app design that makes it easier to understand all your data.

Beyond that, we'll have to wait and see. Personally, I'm really hoping for a better way to understand my Apple Health data.
